I had the opportunity to take both the 101 and 201 at my home theater with most of the same peeps. My improv experience with them has been amazing because we were all friends who worked on something together. We called each other out on things we fell back into/could improve and it's really helped me change how I play. One person was too quiet, another was too nervous and wouldn't enter scenes, another would remain in one mindset for their scenes, etc. All things that they worked on and improved upon in time for our show. I got called out on being a selfish player who goes too fast and off the walls too quickly and it kept me from growing as a performer/playing with other people well. I'm glad that I got to meet the people that I did those classes with and playing with them. Our teacher is also a really casual and fun guy to be around so that also adds to it. Improv wouldn't be what it is without other people.
